To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) in high multiplicity pp events at 900 Ge V the energy from the initial state flux tubes is transferred to the final state hadrons via a hydro-dynamic evolution, and (ii) the initial state flux tube density is proportional to the number of charged particles in a given event.

(1) the energy density from flux tubes can be used as an input for the initial state of hydrodynamics in pp collisions, (2) the hydrodynamic evolution can be followed to the freezeout stage, and (3) the freezeout stage can be simulated using the Cooper-Frye formula with the freezeout surface obtained by the method of Cooper-Frye.
